description_full: Agilent Technologies, Inc. provides application focused solutions to the life sciences, diagnostics, and applied chemical markets worldwide. The company operates through three segments: Life Sciences and Diagnostics Markets, Agilent CrossLab, and Applied Markets. The Life Sciences and Diagnostics Markets segment offers liquid chromatography systems and components; and liquid chromatography mass spectrometry systems. This segment is also involved in the genomics, contract development and manufacturing organization, pathology, companion diagnostics, and biomolecular analysis businesses. The Agilent CrossLab segment provides various services, including repairs, parts, maintenance, installations, training, compliance support, software as a service, asset management, consulting, and other custom services. This segment also offers consumables, including gas chromatography and liquid chromatography columns, sample preparation products, custom chemistries, and various laboratory supplies; software and informatics solutions comprising software for instrument control, data acquisition, data analysis, secure storage of results, and laboratory information and workflow management; and OpenLab laboratory software, an open software platform that enables customers to capture, analyze, and share scientific data throughout the lab and across the enterprise. In addition, it provides automated sample preparation solutions, such as liquid handling, plate management, consumables, and scheduling software. The Applied Markets segment offers products in the areas of gas chromatography, mass spectrometry, spectroscopy, vacuum technology, and remarketed instruments. It markets its products through direct sales, distributors, resellers, manufacturer's representatives, and electronic commerce. Agilent Technologies, Inc. was incorporated in 1999 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

financial_summary: Agilent Technologies, Inc. is a large-cap healthcare business with a $48.0B market cap on $6.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +0% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 18% against a 10% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $1.2B in free cash flow — roughly 17 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.20× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 13× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 1.5%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 2.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 20% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 7% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 33% and a beta of 0.99, it moves roughly with the market.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $79.00 (margin of safety -116%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 20%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $61.14 to $104 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Healthcare peers: P/E 33.6 vs 25.8, EV/EBITDA 24.9 vs 15.3 and P/FCF 41.7 vs 22.3 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 32% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.4% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 2.9% (vs the 8% bar).
The 20 covering analysts target $183 on average, 7% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 18% clears the cost of capital of 9.8% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.37).
It converts 17% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.20x.
ROE of 19% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
It spends 6.5% of revenue on R&D and 1.8% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.9x net debt to EBITDA ($1.8B of cash against $3.4B of debt), with interest covered 13.2x.
Working capital ties up about 128 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
Goodwill makes up 35% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 0.5% over 3 years, 5.4% over 5 years and 5.6% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 14%).
At current returns, reinvesting 22% of profits supports about 4.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 7.5% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.00, a backlog worth 6% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 15%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.4x, 5.9% of sales), a maintenance pace.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and institutions hold 96%.
Shareholder yield is a modest 1.5% (0.9% in buybacks and 0.6% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 1.4% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 14 consecutive years, raising it 4.9% a year over the last five.
